title: As a developer, I can provision an on-demand GPU instance from the console or API and be running code on it within minutes
As a developer, I can start, stop, restart, and terminate instances programmatically and keep paying only for what is running
As an ML engineer, I can set auto-shutdown timers or spend limits so a forgotten instance can't silently run up a huge bill
As an AI agent, I can provision a GPU, monitor it, run a workload, and tear it down end to end through documented APIs, CLI, or MCP without a human in the console
As an AI agent, I can query the GPU catalog with live pricing and availability from a public or documented endpoint before committing any spend
As an ML engineer, I am billed at per-second or per-minute granularity and only while my instance is actually running
As an ML engineer, I can see the published per-GPU-hour price for every GPU type on a public pricing page without talking to sales
As an ML engineer, I can rent spot or interruptible GPU capacity at a deep discount with clearly documented preemption semantics
As a platform engineer, I can lock in reserved or committed-use discounts for sustained GPU capacity
As a platform engineer, I can pull usage and billing breakdowns programmatically to attribute GPU spend by team or workload
As an ML engineer, I can see real-time GPU availability by type and region before I try to provision, instead of discovering stockouts by failure
As a platform engineer, I can see documented quotas and instance limits and raise them through a defined process
As an ML engineer, I can choose from current-generation datacenter GPUs (H100/H200/B200 class) as well as cheaper previous-generation options
As an ML engineer, I can provision a multi-node GPU cluster with fast interconnect for distributed training without a sales cycle
As a platform engineer, I can schedule jobs on managed Slurm or Kubernetes instead of building my own scheduler on raw nodes
As a developer, I can attach persistent network storage that survives instance teardown, so datasets and checkpoints outlive any single GPU rental
As a developer, I can move data in and out efficiently — S3-compatible endpoints, cloud-storage sync, or documented transfer tooling
As a developer, I can launch from pre-built ML templates (PyTorch, CUDA, vLLM, ComfyUI) instead of assembling an environment from scratch
As a developer, I can run my own Docker image or custom machine template with my exact environment
As a developer, I can SSH into my GPU instance with my own keys and get root-level control of the environment
As a developer, I can open Jupyter or connect my IDE (VS Code/Cursor) to the instance in one step
As a developer, I can expose ports to serve applications from my instance and connect instances over private networking
As a developer, I can deploy code to autoscaling serverless GPU workers that scale to zero, instead of managing always-on instances
As a platform engineer, I can manage team members with roles and scoped API keys so credentials and spend stay controlled
As a platform engineer, I can verify the provider's security and compliance posture (SOC 2, data handling, datacenter tiers) before putting proprietary models on it
